title: Ash Pearson, 'The Best 50 Metal Drummers Of All Time', Drumeo Beat (updated 3 May 2023)
notes: Compiled by Revocation drummer Ash Pearson. Ranked list with a short case for each player; quoted claims are used per drummer.

title: Blast beat - Wikipedia
notes: Origins in hardcore and grindcore; Napalm Death and drummer Mick Harris coined the term; Pete Sandoval 'purportedly was the first to use blast beats in metronomic time'.

title: Abe Cunningham - Wikipedia
notes: Deftones drummer; 'known for his frantic, pounding rhythms and clever usage of tempo'; BBC reviewer quote on his expressiveness.

title: Brann Dailor - Wikipedia
notes: Mastodon drummer and vocalist; influences Phil Collins (1970s), Sean Reinert, Mikkey Dee, Dave Lombardo, Elvin Jones, Tony Williams, Billy Cobham, Bill Bruford, Dave Witte.

title: Charlie Benante - Wikipedia
notes: Anthrax and S.O.D. drummer; 'one of the pioneers of double bass drumming and credited with popularizing the blast beat technique' with thrash metal.

title: David Silveria - Wikipedia
notes: Original Korn drummer, 1993-2006; later Infinika.

title: Korn - Wikipedia
notes: Formed 1993 by Shaffer, Arvizu and David Silveria; 'notable for pioneering and popularizing the nu metal genre'. Debut Korn 1994; Follow the Leader 1998.

title: Derek Roddy - Wikipedia
notes: Extreme metal drummer nicknamed 'One Take'; Hate Eternal, Nile, Malevolent Creation, Serpents Rise; auditioned for Dream Theater 2010.

title: Hellhammer (musician) - Wikipedia
notes: Jan Axel Blomberg; Mayhem drummer since 1988, only member on all their studio albums; co-founded Arcturus 1987; three Spellemannprisen.

title: Mayhem (band) - Wikipedia
notes: Pioneers of Norwegian black metal; their music has profoundly influenced the genre; Hellhammer took over the drums with Dead on vocals.

title: Mike Mangini - Wikipedia
notes: Dream Theater 2010-2023; Berklee faculty; five World's Fastest Drummer records 2002-2005; Annihilator, Extreme, Steve Vai; influences Ringo, Buddy Rich, Bozzio, Peart.

title: Mikkey Dee - Wikipedia
notes: Motörhead 1992-2015; Scorpions since 2016; King Diamond, Helloween; influences Peart, Brian Downey, Buddy Rich, Steve Smith, especially Ian Paice; long solos.

title: Paul Bostaph - Wikipedia
notes: Slayer 1992-2001, 2013-2019, 2024; Forbidden, Exodus, Testament; replaced Lombardo; influences Peart, Phil Rudd, Clive Burr.

title: Pete Sandoval - Wikipedia
notes: Terrorizer, Morbid Angel; learned double bass after joining Morbid Angel; AllMusic: 'challenges one's perception of how fast a drummer can possibly drum'; influences Clive Burr, Lombardo, Hoglan, Peart.

title: Vinnie Paul - Wikipedia
notes: Pantera co-founder with Dimebag Darrell; Damageplan, Hellyeah; influences Peter Criss, Alex Van Halen, Tommy Aldridge; four Grammy nominations.

title: Gene Hoglan - Wikipedia
notes: 'The Atomic Clock'; Dark Angel, Death, Strapping Young Lad, Fear Factory, Dethklok, Testament; lengthy double-kick rhythms; Modern Drummer cover 2010; Terrorizer poll 2010; influences Peart, Criss, Cozy Powell, Aldridge, Phil Taylor.

title: Nick Menza - Wikipedia
notes: Megadeth 1989-1998 (Rust in Peace, Countdown to Extinction, Youthanasia, Cryptic Writings); son of Don Menza; influences Buddy Rich, Gadd, Porcaro, Bellson.

title: Dirk Verbeuren - Wikipedia
notes: Belgian; Megadeth, Soilwork; influences Lombardo, Mick Harris, Reinert, Hoglan, Haake; four Toontrack MIDI libraries.

title: Dave Witte - Wikipedia
notes: Municipal Waste, Discordance Axis, Melt-Banana, Burnt by the Sun, Human Remains; session drummer.

title: Tom Hunting - Wikipedia
notes: Exodus drummer and only remaining original member; influences CCR, Bonham, Moon, Peart, Clive Burr.

title: Exodus (band) - Wikipedia
notes: Bay Area thrash pioneers alongside Metallica; Bonded by Blood (1985), Fabulous Disaster (1989).

title: Chris Pennie - Wikipedia
notes: Dillinger Escape Plan co-founder; Coheed and Cambria; influences Ulrich, Copeland, Reinert; cited as influence by Dailor, Christy, Witte, Tyshawn Sorey and many others; triggered electronics live.

title: Matt Garstka - Wikipedia
notes: Animals as Leaders drummer.

title: Animals as Leaders - Wikipedia
notes: Instrumental progressive metal, prominent in djent; Garstka (drums since 2012) calls the style 'metal fusion'.

title: Nick Barker (drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: Cradle of Filth 1993-1999, Dimmu Borgir 1999-2004, Brujeria; influences Peart, Hoglan, Clive Burr, McBrain, Lombardo, Sandoval.

title: Chris Adler - Wikipedia
notes: Lamb of God founding drummer 1994-2019; Megadeth Dystopia (Grammy 2017); Modern Drummer Readers Poll wins; influences Shannon Larkin, Copeland, Bonham, Lombardo, Gar Samuelson, Hoglan.

title: Sean Reinert - Wikipedia
notes: Cynic co-founder, Death (Human), Gordian Knot, Aghora; influences Bonham, Peart, Alex Van Halen, Bozzio, Weckl; cited by Dailor, Hoglan, Verbeuren, Pennie, Kollias, Duplantier and others.

title: George Kollias (drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: Greek; Nile since Annihilation of the Wicked; distinctive foot technique between heel-up and heel-down; teaches at Modern Music School Athens; co-designed Pearl Demon pedals.

title: Paul Mazurkiewicz - Wikipedia
notes: Cannibal Corpse drummer; Dave Lombardo his biggest influence.

title: Cryptopsy - Wikipedia
notes: Montreal death metal; Flo Mounier sat in temporarily in 1992 and stayed; None So Vile (1996) 'an influential cult classic'.

title: Mario Duplantier - Wikipedia
notes: Gojira drummer; 'polyrhythmic patterns and distinctive jazzy fills and drum breaks'; studied at Agostini's school; voted No. 1 metal drummer four times.

title: Eloy Casagrande - Wikipedia
notes: Brazilian; Sepultura 2011-2024; Slipknot since 2024; Modern Drummer Readers Poll Best Metal Drummer 2024; won MD Undiscovered Drummer contest 2006 (Drumeo).

title: Igor Cavalera - Wikipedia
notes: Sepultura co-founder 1984-2006; Cavalera Conspiracy; 'innovative style in the album Chaos A.D. brought tribal elements into the songs', developed further on Roots; influences Roger Taylor, Bill Ward, Lombardo, Copeland.

title: Bobby Jarzombek - Wikipedia
notes: Halford, Riot, Fates Warning, Sebastian Bach, Spastic Ink, George Strait; cymbals positioned behind his shoulders; MIDI groove library; instructional DVD.

title: Raymond Herrera - Wikipedia
notes: Fear Factory founding drummer; 'high speed playing, particularly his "stop go" double bass technique'; Brujeria; games and film composer.

title: Ken Owen - Wikipedia
notes: Carcass founding member and drummer; vocals; Blackstar after 1995; appears on Surgical Steel.

title: Napalm Death - Wikipedia
notes: Grindcore pioneers; Mick Harris joined December 1985; Danny Herrera, a friend of Jesse Pintado, replaced him in 1991.

title: Ben Koller - Wikipedia
notes: Converge, Mutoid Man, Killer Be Killed, All Pigs Must Die, High on Fire.

title: Krisiun - Wikipedia
notes: Brazilian death metal, founded 1990 by brothers Alex Camargo, Moyses Kolesne and Max Kolesne (drums); debut Black Force Domain 1995.

title: Hannes Grossmann - Wikipedia
notes: Necrophagist Epitaph (2004): complex polyrhythmic drumming and blastbeats up to 240 bpm; Obscura; Alkaloid.

title: Scott Travis - Wikipedia
notes: Judas Priest since 1989, Racer X, Thin Lizzy; ambidextrous open-handed; Rock and Roll Hall of Fame 2022 with Judas Priest.

title: Painkiller (Judas Priest album) - Wikipedia
notes: First Priest album with Scott Travis; 'with his heavy use of double kicks, Travis gave Judas Priest a new sound and heavier edge'; speed metal.

title: Les Binks - Wikipedia
notes: Judas Priest 1977-1979 (Stained Class, Killing Machine, Unleashed in the East); 'Exciter' double bass drumming an important early influence on thrash; Loudwire: 'carving metal's future'; RRHOF 2022.

title: Stained Class - Wikipedia
notes: Opener 'Exciter' regarded as an important early influence on thrash metal; Tom G. Warrior: 'a prototype of thrash metal'.

title: Phil Taylor (musician) - Wikipedia
notes: 'Philthy Animal'; Motörhead 1975-1984 and 1987-1992, the classic Lemmy/Clarke/Taylor line-up.

title: Fenriz - Wikipedia
notes: Darkthrone drummer and songwriter with Nocturno Culto; DIY ethic; refuses to play live; focus of Until the Light Takes Us.

title: Darkthrone - Wikipedia
notes: Leading band in Norwegian black metal; A Blaze in the Northern Sky (1992), Under a Funeral Moon (1993), Transilvanian Hunger (1994), the 'Unholy Trinity', among the most influential black metal recordings.

title: Kjetil-Vidar Haraldstad - Wikipedia
notes: Frost; Satyricon and 1349; 'regarded as one of the fastest and most proficient drummers in the black metal and extreme metal genres'; credited as 'battery'.

title: Mick Harris - Wikipedia
notes: Napalm Death 1985-1991; coined 'grindcore'; 'widely regarded as one of the founders of the blast beat'; later Painkiller with Zorn and Laswell, Scorn, Lull.

title: Gar Samuelson - Wikipedia
notes: Megadeth 1984-1987; 'one of the most influential drummers of thrash metal, having pioneered the incorporation of jazz fusion into the subgenre'.

title: Jürgen Reil - Wikipedia
notes: Ventor; Kreator founding drummer; double-bass style of thrash and death metal; sang on early songs ('Riot of Violence').

title: Kreator - Wikipedia
notes: German thrash from Essen; Petrozza and Reil the only original members; Pleasure to Kill (1986) widely considered a thrash classic and a big influence on death metal.

title: Chris Reifert - Wikipedia
notes: Founder, vocalist and drummer of Autopsy; drummer on Death's Scream Bloody Gore; 'a pioneer of the death-doom fusion genre'.

title: Yoshiki (musician) - Wikipedia
notes: Leader, drummer, pianist and main songwriter of X Japan; visual kei; Billboard 'musical innovator'; voted best drummer and best keyboardist by readers and professional musicians in 2018.

title: Girlschool - Wikipedia
notes: Formed in the NWOBHM in 1978; 'the longest-running all-female rock band'; three albums of 'punk-tinged metal' in the early 1980s; associated with Motörhead; an inspiration for many female rock musicians; Denise Dufort an original member.

title: Brant Bjork - Wikipedia
notes: Drummer and founder of 'the influential Californian stoner rock band Kyuss'; Fu Manchu, Vista Chino; 'one of the more notable figures in the stoner rock and Palm Desert scene'.

title: Anvil (band) - Wikipedia
notes: Canadian heavy metal from 1978; founders Lips Kudlow and drummer Robb Reiner; cited as influencing Megadeth, Slayer, Anthrax and Metallica; subject of Anvil! The Story of Anvil (2008).
